brief: Distinguish money received and usable today from an unpaid promise before making a spending decision.

en-US.scenario: Fictional US-dollar examples for "Received or still expected?"; illustrative amounts, not current prices or product offers. No assumption of salary, bank ownership or spare income.

es-MX.scenario: Ejemplos ficticios en pesos mexicanos para "¿Recibido o todavía pendiente?"; montos ilustrativos, no precios vigentes ni ofertas. No se supone nómina, cuenta bancaria ni dinero sobrante.

pt-BR.scenario: Exemplos fictícios em reais para "Recebido ou ainda esperado?"; valores ilustrativos, não preços atuais nem ofertas. Sem supor salário, conta bancária ou dinheiro sobrando.

objective.observable_action: Distinguish money received and usable today from an unpaid promise before making a spending decision.
objective.success_criterion: Complete the fresh-context transfer using only its visible information.

instruction.relevance: A promised payment can help you plan. It is not money you can spend yet.
instruction.misconception: Treating an expected payment as money already available.
instruction.numeracy_support: No arithmetic is assumed. Follow one named person and the payment status.

evidence.reasoning: Ana finishes a repair. Her customer promises payment tomorrow; Ana has not received that money today.
The customer pays Ana in cash. Now she has that money and can include it in today’s amount.
A promise does not put money in your hands today.
This payment is already in your hands.
Money can arrive as cash or in an account. Count it when received and available, not when announced.
The payment is still expected, even with an agreed price.
Available money in the account has already arrived.
An approved refund can still be unpaid. Wait for the money to arrive before counting it as available.
Approval is not the same as receiving the refund.
You spotted a timing gap before relying on future money.

delayed_retrieval.fresh_context: Apply this skill in a later integrated decision with a different constraint.
